title: The Sparrow and the Eagle
summary: From the dizzying heights of a craggy mountain peak, an immense imperial eagle folded his wings, plunged like a thunderbolt into the green meadow below, and seized a fat young l...
full_text:
From the dizzying heights of a craggy mountain peak, an immense imperial eagle folded his wings, plunged like a thunderbolt into the green meadow below, and seized a fat young lamb in his talons, bearing it effortlessly back to his aerie to feed his hungry eaglets.

Sitting upon a nearby hawthorn bush, a tiny brown sparrow observed the majestic feat with eyes burning with envy and foolish ambition. 'What is there in this feat that I cannot accomplish?' chirped the sparrow conceitedly. 'He has feathers, wings, and a beak, and I possess feathers, wings, and a beak! If an eagle can carry a lamb, surely I can carry a full-grown ram!'

Puffing up his tiny breast feathers, the sparrow fluttered high into the air, fluttered his little wings with all his might, and dove down onto the back of a huge ram that was grazing among the clover.

With a triumphant chirp, the sparrow dug his tiny claws into the thick, matted wool of the ram's fleece. But alas! The ram felt nothing more than the landing of a thistle-down, and continued calmly chewing his cud. When the sparrow attempted to lift the massive beast into the sky, he could not stir a single hair. Worse still, when he tried to take flight, his sharp little claws had become hopelessly tangled in the dense, oily curls of the sheep's wool.

The sparrow beat his wings in a frenzy, screeching and fluttering, but he was held fast as if in a spider’s web.

Presently, the shepherd boy walked by carrying his crook. Seeing the frantic little bird thrashing upon the ram’s back, the boy laughed heartily, reached out his hand, and untangled the bird's feet. He clipped the sparrow's flight feathers, placed him in a wicker cage, and took him home to his little sister.

When the girl asked: 'Brother, what kind of bird is this?' the boy laughed: 'If you ask him, he will tell you he is an eagle; but if you look at his wings, you will see he is only a foolish sparrow who mistook his ambition for ability.'
moral: Do not attempt burdens beyond your strength merely out of foolish imitation of the mighty.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Sparrow and the Eagle"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
